name: Goat head (frac head)
function: The flow head on top of the frac tree with two to four inlets where high-pressure lines converge into the well.

tabs.overview:
Named for the horn-like inlets. Each inlet takes a hammer union or a flanged connection from the zipper manifold or missile lines. A top connection may carry a pressure transducer, a bleed, or a cap.

The standard stack on this site uses a flanged inlet block and a spooled treating line instead of a goat head, so the goat head is documented as the hammer-union alternative and is not drawn in the standard tree model.
tabs.engineering: A forged or fabricated pressure-containing block rated with the tree; inlet sizes commonly 3 in. or 4 in.; some designs are flanged big-bore heads that replace multiple inlets with one large line.
tabs.connections: Inlets from the zipper manifold or missile; bottom flange to the swab valve or a spacer spool.
tabs.safety: High-velocity proppant flow at the inlets erodes the head; inspect between wells. Pressurized unions must be restrained.
tabs.operations: Removed for wireline runs on most rig-ups (the lubricator lands on the swab valve or a wellhead adapter) unless a dedicated frac and wireline configuration is used.

hazards.control: Pressure test before pumping; bleed down and verify zero before breaking any connection.
Restraints and whip checks on iron; exclusion zone around pressurized lines.
Tree saver in the wellhead; valves fully open or fully closed only; iron inspection.
